I've outlined my concerns before about the future of Voat, mainly centering around the fact that there is no way that voat is profitable. Looking at the current situation and numbers that Atko has given us I determined that voat could have as little as 83 days remaining.

https://voat.co/v/whatever/comments/1057796

The main finding of the research in that post was there is no possible scenario where voat is profitable. Especially now that we're seeing the advertisement has at best a 50% placement rate.

Note: This was before the FPH donation drive but these numbers can't be updated unless Atko releases any information regarding how much was raised. If they release donation data then I will update my findings

However THIS post is about something else that is troubling

From Atko 2 days ago:

Voat traffic has doubled over the past few days... Daily unique visitors, that is. I was hoping we would be able to cut back on a few things but for now we'll have to keep the machines running to accommodate the new users Source

This comment shows that growth for Voat is problematic. Voat makes the same amount of money regardless of their visitors because they do not have a proper advertising system in place. I've spoken about this in some more detail in this comment chain Source

Voat cannot grow because it costs them more money going forward without giving them any additional benefit. The result is that if Reddit-refugees keep coming over it will hurt voat, not help it, and speed up it's eventual financial death. If the information given to us by the admins are accurate then there is no real future here.

Any site where growth is a problem and not a positive is in trouble.

Reddit will continue to alienate it's userbase through pushes to become more attractive to advertisers and it's financial backers. Voat does not get to determine it's traffic levels and without a profitable and scalable business model they will fail.

The fact is that when your servers burn through $5000+ per month eventually people are going to get tired of opening their wallets so the admins can burn their money and when that happens Voat will come to an end.

The past has shown us that when there is good news companies are more than happy to tell us all about it, Voat is no different. Since we haven't been given any new financial information then I will continue to assume the worst and plan accordingly. My hope is that by drawing attention to these issues they will be addressed and answered, either by users who have information I missed or the Admins.

I'll end this posts by asking people to prove me wrong. I would love to be wrong, I like it here and I like what this site represents.

You're right, but there aren't many clear solutions at this point. Voat knew that there were going to be major financial issues about a year ago when FPH migrated over, These financial problems have been a known issue for close to a year.

These issues required massive amounts of work on the core infrastructure of the site since they were systemic (coding language, database requirements). A rebuild is no small task but they had a year to do it (and we still don't even have an API). Honestly I made this gif to describe how I feel.

Since it would take a complete rebuild to fix the insane server cost problem and that may not be an option this point because well, its today, I would say that changing the advertising policy is the next best option.

I talk about it a bit here: https://voat.co/v/AskVoat/comments/1077859/5385294

Basically Atko is underselling the advertising space based. $55 a day is a massive bargain for anyone who has something to sell but because he refuses to even offer basic metrics (pageviews, clicks) its impossible for anyone serious to even consider the purchase of adspace without knowing if its a good deal or not.

So, changing the advertising policy is the easiest solution, just adding some code to track metrics on the ads and making those public will massively increase the value of that adspace and will get voat a lot closer to breakeven.

I recall that Putt-Putt mentioned recently that some new caching was being implemented that was going to save them a ton, but with the recent influx... ???

Yes, they implemented Redis, which is a tool for making their databases more cost efficient through caching. Voat still uses SQL as their database. Its impossible to know how much this saved them but Redis is not new technology and if it was a significant amount you would have thought they'd have done it much sooner.

Even with a 50% reduction in cost, which is incredibly optimistic, Voat is still a long way off from breakeven (source).
